domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: The authenticated actor and the subject of leave data. Gains a nullable credential (passwordHash) to support login; it is never serialized into any response body.

domain_entities.name: AuthToken
domain_entities.purpose: A stateless JWT bearer credential minted at login. Its payload contract is fixed by the existing auth verifier: sub = employee id, role = EmployeeRole.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: The caller's current-period leave balance per effective policy. `available` is derived, never stored; OPEN vs CLOSED is inferred from periodStart/periodEnd relative to now.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: The effective entitlement rule for a leave type over a time window. A leave type may have several policies over time; exactly one ACTIVE policy applies per leaveTypeCode as of a given date.

business_rules: requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1 (inclusive calendar days, whole-day only, no weekend/holiday exclusion) is the single canonical day-count derivation for every consumer. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever requestedDays / leave day counting appears, not only here]

Date-range filtering is inclusive on both edges (startDate >= from AND startDate <= to, same for endDate). A calendar-day range is inclusive throughout. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequestQueryParams date bounds appears, not only here]

Leave visibility scoping: EMPLOYEE sees only their own requests; MANAGER sees their own plus direct reports (employee.managerId === actor.id), one level only, NOT transitive; ADMIN sees all. The same rule governs both list and single-request reads. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest visibility appears, not only here]

A caller who may not see a leave request receives the SAME response as one that does not exist (indistinguishable 404), so the endpoint cannot be used to probe for ids. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest single-read authorization appears, not only here]

Login failure is indistinguishable: a wrong email and a wrong password produce the same status and message, so the endpoint cannot enumerate accounts. passwordHash is never returned in any response body. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Authentication / login appears, not only here]

The JWT payload contract is fixed: sub = employee id, role = EmployeeRole. This is the contract the existing auth verifier consumes and must not change. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever AuthToken payload appears, not only here]

Accrual-period derivation is shared: startOfUtcDay, addMonths, and periodContaining are pure UTC date arithmetic anchored on the employee's hireDate, with exactly one copy consumed by both the leave and balance paths. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Accrual period derivation appears, not only here]

Effective policy selection: at most one policy per leaveTypeCode — status ACTIVE, effectiveFrom <= asOf, and (effectiveTo IS NULL OR effectiveTo >= asOf); if more than one remains, take the latest effectiveFrom. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeavePolicy effective selection appears, not only here]
available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays, computed (never stored) per balance entry. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance available days appears, not only here]

GET /balances/me returns a LIST of all leave-type balances for the caller's current period, one entry per effective policy, even when it holds one element. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Balance read surface appears, not only here]

Every new route resolves its actor from request.user (never a client-supplied id) and enforces role membership at the API boundary. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Actor resolution / RBAC appears, not only here]
Read endpoints must not write and must not open a transaction. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Read endpoints appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
Domain slice for "Authentication and read endpoints (v2)".

New/changed entities:
- Employee gains `passwordHash: string | null` (nullable credential; never serialized). Lifecycle unchanged: ACTIVE, TERMINATED, ON_LEAVE.
- AuthToken (new): stateless JWT bearer credential. Lifecycle: ISSUED, EXPIRED. Payload contract fixed by existing verifier: sub = employee id, role = EmployeeRole.
- LeaveBalance: `available` is a computed field (entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays), never stored. Lifecycle OPEN/CLOSED inferred from periodStart/periodEnd vs now.
- LeavePolicy: effective-policy selection rule (at most one ACTIVE policy per leaveTypeCode as of a date; latest effectiveFrom wins).

Binding business rules (scope broad):
- requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1 inclusive calendar days (canonical, single source).
- Date-range filtering inclusive on both edges.
- Leave visibility: EMPLOYEE own only; MANAGER own + direct reports (one level, non-transitive); ADMIN all. Same rule for list and single read.
- Indistinguishable 404 for unauthorized vs nonexistent single leave read.
- Indistinguishable login failure (wrong email vs wrong password); passwordHash never returned.
- JWT payload contract fixed (sub/role).
- Accrual-period derivation shared (startOfUtcDay/addMonths/periodContaining, pure UTC, anchored on hireDate).
- available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays.
- GET /balances/me returns a list (one entry per effective policy).
- Actor resolved from request.user, never client-supplied id.
- Read endpoints never write and never open a transaction.

No new lifecycle states beyond existing canonical ones (Employee ACTIVE/TERMINATED/ON_LEAVE; LeaveBalance OPEN/CLOSED; LeavePolicy DRAFT/ACTIVE/SUPERSEDED; AuthToken ISSUED/EXPIRED). No open questions — all boundary/count/range/unit decisions were settled by the feature's DECISIONS ALREADY MADE section.
